title: AccuWeather Forecast: Clouds increase tonight; heavy rain, gusty winds begin overnight - ABC7 Bay Area
text:
AccuWeather Forecast: Clouds increase tonight; heavy rain, gusty winds begin overnight - ABC7 San Francisco 
 24/7 Live San Francisco East Bay South Bay Peninsula North Bay WEATHER 
 AccuWeather Forecast: Clouds increase tonight; heavy rain, gusty winds begin overnight 
 Wednesday, November 18, 2026 12:53AM 
 ABC7 Eyewitness News weather anchor Spencer Christian has the AccuWeather forecast. Takeaway of the Day Today, we are experiencing the calm before yet another storm. Skies have gone from mostly sunny this morning to increasingly cloudy in the afternoon, as tomorrow's storm approaches. Late afternoon temperatures ranged mainly from upper 50s to around 61 degrees across the Bay Area. Late tonight, we can expect clouds to get lower and darker, and light rain ahead of the next storm will begin pushing into the North Bay shortly after midnight.
 A Look Ahead Tomorrow's storm will be a strong Level 3 on the Storm Impact Scale . Heavy rain and gusty winds will begin pounding the North Bay between midnight and 3 a.m., and the storm will spread southward and eastward onto the Peninsula and East Bay just as the morning commute is beginning. Commuters should be prepared for heavy downpours, wind gusts up to or above 35 miles per hour, and ponding or localized flooding on roadways.
 A WIND ADVISORY will be in effect for most of the Bay Area tomorrow and a HIGH WIND WARNING for the East Bay Hills. In the hills, Gusts could exceed 50 miles per hour.
 This storm will continue drenching the Bay Area through tomorrow night and into Thursday, by which time it will be ranked at Level 2- still an impactful storm.
 In addition to flooding concerns from the heavy rain, wave heights are increasing again, and a HIGH SURF ADVISORY will be in effect from 4 p.m. tomorrow to 4 p.m. Thursday. Breakers may reach heights of 18 feet, and there is an increasing risk of dangerous sneaker waves and rip currents.
